beginner.headline: Tomorrow (Thu Oct 8): not recommended for beginner lessons. Flood Watch for Oʻahu runs through Thursday afternoon with heavy showers, isolated thunderstorms and south (onshore) wind, and brown water at Waikīkī is likely after tonight's rain. Evening forecast, so confidence is lower than a morning report; the morning on-site check decides.
beginner.recommendation: Plan to cancel or reschedule Thursday lessons. Only reconsider if tomorrow morning shows the heavy rain missed town, the water at Canoes is visibly clear (no brown, gray or cloudy water), no thunder is heard, and the wind is lighter than forecast. Even then, keep it to a single strong adult student late in the day. Friday looks better on weather (partly sunny, light south wind) but runoff can linger; recheck then.

alerts.details: Deep tropical moisture pulled north by a strengthening low about 750 miles north of Kauaʻi. Heavy showers and thunderstorms moving over Oʻahu from the south this evening; flood threat through at least Thursday morning; whole island at risk, leeward areas most prone.

watch.head: Brown water likely at Waikīkī Thursday
watch.body: Heavy rain tonight usually means runoff from the Ala Wai and storm drains. DOH guidance is to stay out of storm-runoff water and that coastal water usually takes about 48 hours to flush. No Waikīkī advisory was verified; that is not proof the water is clean.
